plan: With 3 bidders total, values uniform on [0,49], the standard symmetric equilibrium bid in a first-price auction is (n-1)/n * value = (2/3)*value. My value is $10, so optimal bid ≈ $6.67. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin, since bidding my full value would yield zero profit even if I win, while bidding too low risks losing to others. I'll bid slightly rounded to increments of $0.1.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is value*(n-1)/n = 30*(2/3) = 20. This balances the probability of winning against the profit margin, maximizing expected payoff. I'll bid $20 to follow this optimal strategy since no other history is available to adjust from.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $25, so I'll bid approximately $16.7 to optimize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.
